question.text: What will Democrats' lead be in the congressional generic ballot on the eve of Election Day 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the net support lead for Democrats shown at the Silver Bulletin's [Who’s ahead on the generic congressional ballot?](https://www.natesilver.net/p/generic-ballot-average-2026-nate-silver-bulletin-congress-polls) tracker for November 2, 2026, rounded to the nearest tenth, when accessed by Metaculus on or after November 3, 2026.
question.fine_print:
If no value for the exact date is shown, then the closest value preceding it will be used to resolve the question.

Between the value shown in the chart and the csv file under the chart ("Get the data"), the csv file takes precedence. See the "net" column in the csv. 

***
This question's information (resolution criteria, fine print, background info, etc) is synced with an [original identical question](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/46189) which opened on 2026-10-18 12:00:00. This question will resolve based on the resolution criteria and fine print of the linked original question. However, if this question would resolve differently than the original question, then this question will be annulled. Additionally, if the original question's resolution could have been known before this question opened, then this question will be annulled.

research:
## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-23: The Silver Bulletin tracker shows **D +9.1**, with a cycle high of D +9.2 noted on the page. The update says Democrats' September surge "leveled off for a short time, but they're now back on the upswing." I could only see the page text. I could not open the CSV ("net" column), so I don't have the daily values. [Silver Bulletin](https://www.natesilver.net/p/generic-ballot-average-2026-nate-silver-bulletin-congress-polls)
- 2026-10-16: The earlier update put the lead at D +8.9, with the cycle high then at D +9.1. The likely-voter version on the forecast page was D +9.6. That version is not the one that resolves the question. (question background)

## 2. Current status
- The question is not settled. The resolution value is the November 2 entry, about 8 days after the latest reading I could see. The current level is around D +9.1, near the cycle high.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-25: Media reports say the Silver Bulletin model gives Democrats a 95% chance of winning the House. [Times Now](https://www.timesnownews.com/world/us/us-midterm-elections/us-midterm-elections-2025-who-will-win-polls-forecasts-projection-republicans-democrats-house-senate-race-article-156400243)
- 2026-10-24: An MSNBC podcast cites a New York Times poll with Democrats ahead by 11 points. A Mediaite article reports a NYT/Siena poll at 50-39 (D +11), up from D +5 in January. I could not confirm the release date. [Mediaite](https://www.mediaite.com/media/news/shock-ny-times-poll-shows-gop-getting-absolutely-smoked-on-generic-congressional-ballot-trailing-dems-by-double-digits/)
- 2026-10-21: ActiVote (Oct 15-21) has D 53.7 to R 46.3, or D +7.4. ActiVote calls this a cycle high, up from D +6.6 on Oct 14. [ActiVote](https://www.activote.net/polls/generic-ballot/2026-10-21/)
- 2026-10-21: The Decision Desk HQ average is about D +7.9. [DDHQ](https://votes.decisiondeskhq.com/polls/generic-ballot/national)
- 2026-10-23: State polls also look strong for Democrats: Virginia House ballot D +20 (State Navigate, Oct 17-20) and New Hampshire generic ballot D +9 (Saint Anselm, Oct 19-20). [Center Square](https://www.thecentersquare.com/virginia/article_485bd6cb-0e71-4457-b19e-8931dae871a2.html), [Seacoast Online](https://www.seacoastonline.com/story/news/politics/2026/10/23/nh-democrats-lead-election-polls-pappas-shaheen-dilorenzo-sununu-ayotte-warmington/92394297007/)
- 2026-10-13: NewsNation/DDHQ (Oct 5-9) has 49-42, or D +7. [The Hill](https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6143963-democrats-lead-congressional-ballot-ddhq/)
- 2026-09-15: NYT/Siena had D +8.5 among likely voters. [Political Wire](https://politicalwire.com/2026/09/15/democrats-hold-big-lead-on-generic-ballot/)

## 4. Base rates and trend
- The Silver Bulletin average moved from about D +8.9 (Oct 16, and again Oct 20 per search summaries) to D +9.1 (Oct 23). Over the past week or so the drift was about +0.2 points, and the cycle high is D +9.2.
- Earlier this cycle the average was about D +5.5 to 5.6 in the spring and summer. Kalshi weekly markets for 4/24-5/1 and 9/4-9/11 settled "above 5.5/5.6," and the 8/14-8/21 market priced "above 6.8" at only 2%. The surge to about D +9 happened in September and October.
- Silver's average moves slowly. Late in a cycle, a typical 10-day change is a few tenths of a point, and a 1-point move would be unusual. A cluster of high-quality final polls can shift it by about 0.5. This is a rough estimate of my own, not a published statistic.
- Other averages are lower: DDHQ about D +7.9, and uspollingdata about D +7.4 (low confidence in that source). Silver sits at the high end.

## 5. Other forecasts and markets (prices as of 2026-10-25 14:02 UTC)
- Kalshi, "Generic congressional ballot today (Oct 25)": 8.4% is priced at 0.89. That is well below Silver's 9.1, so this market probably uses a different source, likely RealClearPolitics or VoteHub. **It does not match the resolution source.**
- Kalshi weekly "Democrats Up/Down (10/23-10/30), above 8.4%": 0.80. Again, this is probably a different source.
- Kalshi, final House popular vote margin: D 8-10% at 0.26, D 10-12% at 0.23, D 6-8% at 0.14, D 12-14% at 0.12. This is a related question, not the resolution value.
- Kalshi, House popular vote minus the final VoteHub generic ballot: centered near zero, with "R+0.9 to D+0.9" at 0.28.
- I did not find any Polymarket or Manifold market on the Silver Bulletin November 2 value.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The last wave of national polls before Election Day (NYT/Siena, CNN/SSRS, Washington Post, Fox, Marist, Emerson, and others) usually comes out in the final 7-10 days and will feed the November 2 value.
- Silver's average may weight likely-voter results. The final pollster releases switching to likely-voter samples could push the number higher, since the likely-voter version is currently D +9.6.
- Any late news shock in the last week before the November 3 election could also move it.
- The CSV "net" value for November 2 decides the question, and it could differ by a tenth or so from the rounded number in the page text.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** The resolving value is the November 2 entry. Metaculus will check it on or after November 3, so that is about 8 to 9 days from now. The value covers about 10 days of movement from the latest reading.

(b) **Latest known value:** D +9.1 on the Silver Bulletin tracker, dated 2026-10-23. The cycle high is D +9.2, and the page text says Democrats are "back on the upswing."

(c) **If nothing changed:** The answer would be about 9.1.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** The average rose about 0.2 points in a week (8.9 to 9.1), so the trend points to roughly 9.3 to 9.5. A recent NYT/Siena poll at D +11 and an ActiVote poll at a cycle high (D +7.4) both lean slightly upward.

(e) **Historical variation:** Silver's average moves slowly. Over 10 days late in a cycle, a few tenths of a point is typical. A move of about 1 point is unusual but possible if a cluster of final high-quality polls lands on one side.

(f) **Experts and markets:** No market tracks this exact source. Kalshi's daily and weekly generic ballot markets (about 8.4) appear to use a different, lower average. DDHQ is about D +7.9. Silver's likely-voter version is D +9.6, but that version does not resolve this question. Final polls switching to likely-voter samples may nudge the resolving average up slightly.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** A late Republican-favorable news event, plus final polls from Fox, Emerson and Rasmussen-type pollsters tightening to around D +5 to 6, pulls the average down to about D +8 or below.
- **High:** Final waves from NYT, CNN, WaPo and Marist all show double-digit Democratic leads, pushing the average to about D +10.5 or above.
